moon.name: South Pole (Shackleton rim)
moon.blurb: The pole itself sits on the rim of Shackleton crater.

moon.name: Shackleton Crater
moon.blurb: A 21 km crater whose floor has not seen sunlight for billions of years.

moon.name: de Gerlache Rim
moon.blurb: An Artemis III candidate region on the rim of de Gerlache crater.

moon.name: Shoemaker Rim
moon.blurb: Rim of a 51 km crater with a permanently shadowed floor.

moon.name: Faustini Rim
moon.blurb: An Artemis III candidate region on the rim of Faustini crater.

moon.name: Haworth Rim
moon.blurb: Rim of Haworth, a named Artemis III candidate region.

moon.name: Sverdrup Rim
moon.blurb: Rim of Sverdrup crater, between Shackleton and the far side.

moon.name: Malapert Massif
moon.blurb: A tall mountain massif and Artemis III candidate region.

moon.name: Nobile Rim
moon.blurb: Rim of a 73 km crater; Nobile Rim is an Artemis III candidate region.

earth.name: Haughton Crater
earth.blurb: A 23 km impact crater in the High Arctic, home of the NASA Haughton-Mars Project since 1997.

earth.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
earth.blurb: The largest ice-free region of Antarctica, a long-standing NASA analog for polar exploration.

earth.name: Peary Land
earth.blurb: One of the northernmost land areas on Earth, at 82.5° N.

earth.name: Adventdalen
earth.blurb: Arctic valley near Longyearbyen; Svalbard has hosted the NASA-supported AMASE analog expeditions.

earth.name: Askja
earth.blurb: Volcanic caldera where Apollo astronauts trained in 1965 and 1967.

earth.name: Sudbury Basin
earth.blurb: Ancient impact structure used for Apollo 16 and 17 geology training.

earth.name: Nördlinger Ries
earth.blurb: A 24 km impact crater where the Apollo 14 crew trained in 1970.

earth.name: Meteor Crater
earth.blurb: A 1.2 km impact crater used for Apollo astronaut geology training.

earth.name: Mauna Kea
earth.blurb: Volcano slopes used for NASA lunar resource-extraction field tests.
